expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Amended tickets.md (TKT-014..TKT-016, intro + non-goals in the header) and cli.md (CLI-010..CLI-012; CLI-001 and CLI-006 amended). Final message: 'Overdue is a ticket rule next to the TKT-005 due time, and the new command belongs on the CLI surface, so a new file would fragment both.'

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'A ticket that is not closed and is past its due time is overdue, see TKT-014. Support agents use overdue to find the tickets that missed their service-level target...'. 'Prefix: `TKT`.' follows. 'Overdue support does not include these:' lists 5 boundaries (no notifications/escalation, no TKT-005/business-hours change, no late-close report, no filters, no due-time display).

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 6 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. TKT-014 (5 sentences + TODO) and CLI-011 (5 sentences + TODO) are longer than typical.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' with a 4-line example. Filter: TKT-016 'only the tickets that are overdue'. Order: TKT-016 'due time ascending... ID ascending'. Exact due: TKT-014 'At the due time exactly, the ticket is not overdue.' Closed: TKT-014 'never overdue' + TODO. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; the exit code is also flagged with an inline TODO ('confirm that the exit code is 0 whether or not overdue tickets exist') and questions.md Q7.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). Outcomes are CLI lines and exit codes.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is not a state, and the log never records it. Each command computes overdue from the current time when it runs... LOG-009 covers states and due times, not overdue.' TKT-015: 'No event is appended when a ticket becomes overdue.' CLI-012: 'appends no event'. INV-001/INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014: 'TKT-005 sets the due time.' Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'; CLI-010: 'The line of a ticket that is not overdue is unchanged from CLI-006' and its example shows overdue tickets 1 and 3 interleaved in ID order. Order not redefined; no explicit 'order stays' sentence.
